gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the INVZI MagHub Quad Max's three 18.5-inch screens run on a Racertech display driver that Windows installs automatically but macOS needs installed by hand once, that it supports Intel and Apple Silicon Macs, and that its stated fit is 12 to 18-inch laptops with a dual USB-A fallback when the laptop's USB-C has no display output.
standout_why: I read deal.ai's MagHub comparison, The Office Journal's attachable page and itechguides' 15-extender page. deal.ai already says the MagHub Quad Max 'Needs display driver install and 45W USB-C PD power' and lists macOS and Windows, so the driver fact is half there; it lacks the driver's name, the Windows/macOS split, the fit range and the USB-A fallback. The Office Journal and itechguides name no 18 or 18.5-inch extender at all (their screens run 13.3 to 16 inches) and neither states the one-external-display limit on base M1/M2/M3 MacBooks. I could not open the FOPO S999 or tutt.ca S999 pages (HTTP 429 on every attempt), so I cannot say what those two results state about their own video path.
decides: It confirms a split rather than a pick. The one 18.5-inch triple I could source (INVZI MagHub Quad Max) is driver-based, so it suits a laptop that cannot drive three screens natively, and its fit range is stated as 12 to 18 inches. UPERFECT's own store shows its 18.5-inch stacked touch model (BE185CF, formerly Delta Max) as unavailable on 2026-11-21, with a pre-order note. The two FOPO rows we could link are not verified by this angle: the S999's fit range, video path and OS list were unreadable today, and the S788's '12–18.5-inch laptops, UsbDisplay driver required' comes from Dealectric's existing record, which I did not re-read. Both need a successful read of fopomonitor.com before the page states them.
candidates: FOPO S788 16-inch Triple (FOPO fit range 12–18.5-inch laptops, per Dealectric's record)
